subject: Next steps — VPC/data stewardship constraints & air-gap options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Mukherjee <priya.mukherjee@medsecure.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — VPC/data stewardship constraints & air-gap options

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive.

Key pain points you called out:
- PHI must remain in US-only tenancy and cannot cross public internet egress from compute nodes.
- Outbound connections from inference hosts are restricted; only jump-proxy/bastion or approved egress IPs allowed.
- Regulatory need for HSM-backed key management (FIPS 140-2).
- Audit evidence (SOC 2, audit logs) and short log retention (30–90 days depending on dataset) to limit PHI exposure.

Primary goals we captured:
1) Pilot: run 2 curated open models behind a VPC-resident Redwood Private control plane; no internet egress from inference hosts.
2) Latency target: 150–250ms P95 for user-facing inference (short prompts).
3) Security posture: HSM for keys, KMS integration, and per-request audit logs retained for 30 days for the pilot.

Constraints/unknowns we still need from you:
- Confirmation on whether a site-to-site VPN or ExpressRoute (Azure) will be used for control-plane API access — that determines our connector architecture.
- List of exact egress ports/IPs allowed for telemetry/patching windows (we can provide minimal-IP ranges).
- Procurement timeline and any contracting constraints for an initial 6–8 week pilot.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm VPN type (site-to-site vs cloud interconnect) and provide contact for network engineering.
- Redwood (Ben/Jordan/Irene): schedule a 60‑minute technical alignment with your infra/security team to map out network flows and KMS requirements.
- Attach: medsecure_network_diagram.pdf (we put a stub of the diagram you shared in the call notes).

Are you available for the tech align on Friday 18 Sep, morning PT? If that works, Ben will send a calendar invite and we will prepare a short checklist to walk through (ports, subnets, proxy flow, proxy certs, and HSM access model).

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — VPC/data stewardship constraints & air-gap options

Thanks, Irene — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side and answers to your asks: 

Clarifications/requirements:
- We will require FIPS 140-2 validated HSM for key management (on-prem HSM is preferred; cloud HSM must meet FIPS and be dedicated).
- No outbound internet from inference nodes except for a controlled management channel to Redwood control plane via our approved egress IPs.
- Audit logs: for PHI datasets we mandate 30-day retention for the pilot; longer retention (90 days) will be handled post-pilot with legal approval.
- All data-at-rest must be encrypted; customer-managed keys preferred.

Answers to your unknowns:
- We intend to use a site-to-site VPN over our firewall appliance to connect to vendor control planes. We will confirm VPN termination IPs after our network team verifies routing.
- Egress/ports: we can permit a small set of outbound IPs (list to follow); SSH to bastion is permitted from our jump-bucket only.
- Procurement: target to sign a pilot SOW by end of Oct; procurement contact (procurement@medsecure.health) copied here.

I've attached initial_vendor_questions.xlsx with a few compliance and procurement-focused items — Ben, Jordan, can you take a look and flag any redlines we should expect?

We are available for a tech call on Friday 18 Sep at 09:00 PT. Please send invite and agenda.

Thanks,
Priya Mukherjee
Director, IT Security
MedSecure Health
priya.mukherjee@medsecure.health
